judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Medill Plan' is an unexplained proper name and the rules of eligibility are left to be posted rather than stated, so the letter fixes no substantive entitlement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H and 13-I govern the joint Welfare and Pension Funds and 22-F/22-G the Times plans; where this plan fits among them is unexplained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable period of time designated by the employee' and 'a written assignment satisfactory to the Publisher' are both open-ended conditions on the deduction right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.1 and 2-N.3 govern other payroll deductions with tighter mechanics; consistent but differently drawn.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prohibits the subcontracting of bargaining unit deliveries except as it may exist pursuant to the contract' is circular — the exception refers back to the contract whose meaning is in issue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-E freezes methods and extent of delivery, 3-F frees new routes, 12-A regulates wholesalers, and 2-E.2(h) permits other carriers; this 'clarification' does not resolve how those fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Continue its present practice' incorporates an unstated practice, while the annual statement obligation is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-B addresses Times vacation checks and tax deductions and 13-I concerns Pension Fund shifts; the shift statement obligation complements 13-I.1 without conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Every obligation is conditioned on an unscheduled event ('when the planned DEC System is installed and operational'), leaving the timing wholly indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to shifts 'for which contributions were not made' presupposes credited shifts without contributions, which is in tension with 13-I.1's obligation to contribute for each shift worked in the unit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except if delayed because of an emergency or Act of God' is an open excuse attached to an otherwise precise deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A.1 sets the first-year rates effective March 31, 1981 while the Agreement was executed in October 1981, so retroactivity is contemplated and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A preamble reciting that a sub-committee 'discussed and agreed upon the following'; the mixture of discussion and agreement is itself uncertain as to what is binding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is dated November 3, 1978 yet reproduced in the 1981–84 book, relying on the blanket continuation memorandum for force.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recorded as a request and an advisement ('was advised that such vans would be ordered') rather than a promise, so whether it binds is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-K obliges the Publisher to furnish delivery equipment, but this item's status as an obligation depends on the ambiguous preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Would explore the purchase and use of dehumidifiers' creates no enforceable duty and the concern is described rather than remedied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1 imposes a substantive duty against undue hardship and hazard, which this item neither implements nor limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Paid the same as the men in the New York plant for handling three-part inserts (500 or more)' is definite in comparator but silent on what the New York rate is.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A's rate tables do not distinguish plants, so an equal-pay commitment between plants is either redundant or evidence of a practice outside the schedules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure statement of fact ('the Company indicated that new trucks had been ordered'), with no obligation created at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else turns on it; 3-K's equipment duty is unaffected.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sixers' is undefined trade shorthand and the measure is 'the same percentage as they are currently available', an unrecorded baseline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D governs Newspoint conditions and its supersession clause (VIII) may or may not displace this November 1978 letter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Five jobs would be defined when posted (Job Clarification)' promises definition without supplying it, and the jobs are named only by label.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B governs posting of situations and the posting side letter governs job descriptions; this adds a third, vaguer obligation on the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement merely 'to meet and discuss', with no timing or outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-L and 21-D.V deal with commercial and advertising matter substantively; this leaves that subject open despite them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A thirty-day meeting commitment about unspecified 'shop level problems'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16 already channels plant-level disputes; this adds an informal layer without conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same ambiguous 'discussed and agreed upon' preamble as its News counterpart, and the text is scrambled with the heading displaced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dated November 3, 1978 but carried into the 1981–84 book through the blanket continuation memorandum, whose effect is itself unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete: two named jobs, one on each shift.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's control-room provision requires console personnel to be Journeymen and the Supplementary Agreement adds a utility man to relieve the console; complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific as to days, start time and bidding method.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2 and 22-D govern over-the-road runs and transfer points, and Atlantic City lies outside the Metropolitan Area, so the run's terms depend on those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reviewed within a reasonable time' is softened but then capped at sixty days; the review has no stated outcome or standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Supplementary Agreement fixes combined floor hires at eighty-one including the 43rd Street plant, so a later open-ended manning review sits against that fixed number.
